exercises.name: Belt Squat
exercises.desc: A squat where the load hangs from a belt around your hips instead of sitting on your back. Your legs do all the work while your spine stays unloaded, so it's a great way to get heavy quad and glute volume when your back is tired, sore or still recovering from heavy deadlifts. Where you put the pressure in your feet decides which muscle takes the bias: more on the heels for glutes, more towards the toes for quads.
steps: Clip the chain to the belt and fasten the belt snugly across your hips, below the belly button, with the chain hanging straight down between your legs.
Step onto the platform with your feet about shoulder width apart and toes turned out slightly. Line the chain up so it hangs directly under your hips.
Hold the handles or rails for balance, stand tall, then release the machine's safety catch.
Take a breath, brace, and sit straight down between your heels, letting your knees travel forward over your toes. Keep your chest up and torso upright.
Go as deep as you can while keeping your hips tucked under you and your feet flat.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top. Re-set the safety catch when the set is done.
cues: Keep even pressure through the middle of your foot: big toe, little toe and heel all down
Brace your trunk hard before every rep and keep it braced all the way up
Shift a little more onto your heels to bias the glutes
Shift a little more towards your toes to bias the quads
Sit straight down between your heels, not back like a box squat
Use the handles for balance only. Don't pull yourself up with your arms

workouts.title: Full body — First session
workouts.notes: A friendly first session. Focus on positions, not load. Note any movement that feels off.

workouts.title: Lower A — Squat strength
workouts.notes: Warm up for 10 minutes: bike and bodyweight squats. Work up to your top sets and leave 1–2 reps in the tank.

workouts.title: Run — Tempo day
workouts.notes: Easy warm-up, then hold your tempo pace. Finish with core.

workouts.title: Upper A — Push & pull
workouts.notes: Two presses, two pulls, shoulders and arms. Rest fully on the first two lifts.
